title: Connection
description: A configured link between OpenEngine and one account at an external provider. Nothing here is secret: credentials are held in a secret store and only referenced.

connection.description: Snapshot of a connection as `get` and `list` return it. A deleted connection keeps its ID and is still returned by `get` with state `deleted`, so historical jobs and audit records that reference it stay readable.

name.description: The Connection resource's `metadata.name`, unique among connections that are not deleted.

provider.description: Integration provider, such as `github`, `slack` or `linear`. The set of providers is open; an unknown provider is rejected with UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY.

external_account.description: The account at the provider this connection acts for. `id` is the provider's own stable identifier and need not be a subject token.

credential_ref.description: Pointer to a credential in a secret store. The secret itself never crosses this interface.

version.description: Pinned secret version; omitted means the store's current version.

scope.description: What the connection may act on at the provider. `all` covers everything the credential can reach; `selected` only the listed provider resources (for example `owner/repo`).

settings.description: Provider-specific, non-secret configuration. Its shape is defined with the provider ingress/egress contracts, which are deferred; until then it is an object of at most 64 keys.

state.description: Lifecycle state. active: accepts new integration activity. disabled: accepts none, keeps configuration and bindings. deleted: configuration removed; the record remains for history.

health.description: Observed health, independent of lifecycle state. A degraded connection stays active.

in_flight_on_disable.description: What happens to deliveries already accepted when the connection is disabled. drain (default): finish them; accept nothing new. hold: pause them and resume on re-enable; any held delivery that cannot be retained is failed explicitly with PROVIDER_ERROR, never dropped.

in_flight_on_delete.description: What happens to deliveries accepted but not finished when the connection is deleted. reject (default): refuse the delete with INVALID_STATE while any remain. fail: fail each of them explicitly, report the count, then delete.
